notes: Approximate planning model, not unique-person census. Smaller language inputs mix dates and omit diaspora; Catalan source may conflate native and total; use rounded 38 percent.
Arabic standard written access is a separate scenario, not native-speaker coverage.
Chinese scripts and Portuguese variants counted once.
No estimate of deduplicated multilingual union is available.

recommended_statement_before_finalizatio: The33-locale baseline remains an inherited rough38% native-language proxy. The3pilots are not registered or credited as delivered. If all3finalize, a conservative-scope mixed-date speaker-count scenario adds about410million (~5percentagepoints), taking that proxy to about43%. This is not newly reached unique people.
recommended_statement_after_all_three_fi: Hindi, Urdu and Swahili raise the rough native-language planning proxy from about38% to about43%, using narrower Hindi census self-identification; unique readable-user coverage and net-new reach remain unmeasured.
limitations: Existing baseline inputs inherited, not independently re-audited: mixed dates/geographies, Catalan total/native ambiguity, missing diaspora; approximate38% only.
No native/online finalized quality certification inferred from presence of33 registered catalogs; three pilots remain unregistered and conditional.
New figures mix2011India,2023Pakistan,2021Swahili with2026world denominator; neither a2026language census nor a lower bound on current readable users.

Hindi group includes Bhojpuri, Rajasthani and many other classified mother tongues; Hindi translation is not certification of serving every such language. Narrow self-report category also does not test standard Hindi proficiency.

Hindi Devanagari, Urdu Arabic-derived Perso-Arabic/Nastaliq written form and Swahili contemporary Latin standard require reading ability; speech intelligibility does not imply literacy in these scripts. No RomanHindi/RomanUrdu/SwahiliAjami coverage claimed.
Hindi/Urdu spoken overlap does not make the two written translations redundant or guarantee cross-script reading. No script literacy adjustment measured.
Existing English/French/Arabic users overlap new Hindi/Urdu/Swahili audiences; no cross-language unique-person union data or net-new-access count available.
Mother tongue categories are mostly exclusive census responses, but baseline mixes national/global estimates; native multilinguals and methodological overlap remain.

Swahili200m total and baselineArabic335mL2 are not added to L1 scenario. Arabic remains a separately labelled mixed written-access illustration with unmeasured overlap, not a stronger native coverage estimate.
No geographic totals are counted as all literate speakers; Swahili Tanzania/Kenya populations not substituted for L1. Diaspora and L2 access may increase audience but are unquantified.
Remaining27backlog languages not re-audited or credited.
